Great seafood restaurant on the boarder of District 1/3
Aug 2019 • Couples
The great seafood restaurant was just round the corner from where we were staying on the boarder of D1 and D3. We were after some rice and seafood but it was a bit late but Ken’s was still open with a few people still sat outside eating so we went in and looked at the extensive menu. A Hugh selection of different seafood dishes done in a verity of styles and sauces. We ordered some lovely prawns, morning glory and egg fried rice to take away. All prepared fresh and ready in 10 minutes. Great food and good value.

Was thereafter reading review. We are a group of 8 and was ushered to the 2nd floor since it was full on the ground level. The food and staff were nice. However we were served very very slow. We ended up with one dish not served.

Amazing Collection of Snails and Seafood
Jun 2017 • Solo
When I arrived there, there were local clients, which was a great sign for me. I sat on a table, they were already closing (I arrived like 10:30pm), but they served me with a big smile regardless of that. They also put a wonderful playlist on a screen, which created a very pleasant atmosphere. 
Then, I ate noodles with snail, filled with garlic and onions, absolute tasty material. Then, I ate quail eggs in a tamarind sauce. I'll admit I was scared at first because I have never eaten anything like that. But that was just the first blush, because the first bite it proved to have a very rich flavour. I also drank kumquat juice, ice tea, and lemonade. I loved those except for the ice tea. That might be because of the different taste, since it had nothing wrong with it.

Overall, the staff was very friendly, and I'll definitely come back here for more feasts!

Wonderful food
Jun 2017 • Couples
The restaurant was full of locals when we went in, which was a good sign, as we did not want to go to a restaurant that was targeted at tourists.

We ordered a few dishes for a late dinner:
1. Water morning glory
2. Grilled prawns with duck egg sauce
3. Seafood noodles
4. Frog porridge

The dishes all tasted fantastic, other than the frog, which was in my opinion overcooked or not fresh.

Would recommend this restaurant if you have the luxury of time (note: it takes pretty long for each dish to be served)

Food good, service awful!
Mar 2017 • Couples
Lovely food, shame about the terrible service. We went here as it was close to our hotel, looked ok when we passed earlier in the day, so we checked out the reviews which were favourable. We saw ourselves to a table on arrival which was fine. First waitress we saw looked as grumpy as, we checked we were ok sitting where we were, to which we received a cursory grunt. We were shown the menu and given plenty of time to choose, there is a big choice. In the end we both ordered shell fish, a rice each, some stir fried morning glory and a corn and shrimp side dish, and two beers. 
Beers came first, that was good. Then they brought us our morning glory side dish - but nothing else. After waiting a bit we started to tuck in as it was going cold, then my scallops and quails egg dish came, but nothing else. By the time I finished my scallops, my husbands conch type shell fish came, but nothing else. The rice finally came, once everything else was more or less finished, and our corn and shrimp side dish never materialised. We then waited some time before asking for the bill, just in case the last dish arrived. Eventually we gave up, got our bill, which was hard to check as it was all in Vietnamese, the prices didn't all quite match the menu and we weren't entirely certain whether we paid for the non-existent dish or not, but pretty sure not. Still at 280,000 dong (about £12) it was not bad value and the food was excellent. I would not return however as the service was so poor, and we did not feel at all welcome.

It's More than Snails
Mar 2017 • Business
The litteral translation of the name is Ken's Snails but the menu offers so much more. I have never enjoyed fried chicken feet as much anywhere else. There is also a variety of shellfish like conch, Saigon's signature cockles, clams, oysters, scallops, and more. 

The proprietor speaks English and is very helpful. The location is just down the street from the famous Nguyen Kim Electronics Store and a short walk to centrally located Ben Than Market and many city attractions. Free Parking
